rows.subtopic: Elementary Operations and Inverse of a Matrix
rows.text:
Let \(A\) be a \(2 \times 2\) matrix such that

\(A^2 + A + \begin{pmatrix} 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 \end{pmatrix}\).

Let \(I\) denote the \(2 \times 2\) identity matrix. Which of the following statements is correct?
options: \(A\) is invertible but \(A + I\) may not be invertible.
\(A + I\) is invertible but \(A\) may not be invertible.
Neither \(A + I\) nor \(A\) may be invertible.
